title: On-Prem Observability Runbook & Terraform Notes
content:
Purpose:
This working runbook collects playbook fragments, Terraform module notes, and an upgrade plan for deploying the observability stack into private Redwood environments (VPC and on-prem clusters). Aim: a reproducible, secure, upgradeable observability setup covering Prometheus/Grafana, OpenTelemetry (OTEL) collectors, and log shipping (FluentBit/Fluentd or vector).

Scope:
- Kubernetes-based customer clusters (EKS/GKE/AKS or private k8s on-prem).
- VPC-networked private control plane that cannot directly reveal customer data externally.
- Integrations: remote-write to Redwood metrics aggregator (optional), Grafana dashboards (self-hosted), Loki/Elastic for logs, OTEL for traces.
- Excludes: full CI/CD pipeline details — those live in terraform-cicd notes.

High-level architecture (textual):
- Agent layer: OTEL Collector DaemonSet, node agents (FluentBit) for logs, node-exporter / cadvisor for host metrics.
- Scrape layer: Prometheus Operator with ServiceMonitors in monitoring namespace.
- Storage/visualization: Thanos or remote-write to Redwood-hosted bucket if customer approves; Grafana instance in monitoring namespace.
- Networking: internal LB for Grafana (no public IP), Prometheus remote-write over mTLS to Redwood endpoints if configured.

Prerequisites checklist (before terraform apply):
- Cluster kubeconfig with admin privileges stored in secure vault.
- CNI network policies reviewed for monitoring traffic on ports 4317 (OTLP/gRPC), 4318 (OTLP/HTTP), 9411 (zipkin, optional), 9090 (Prometheus), 3000 (Grafana).
- KMS key available for any secret encryption used by modules.
- Namespace "redwood-observability" reserved and team-approved.
- Secrets storage: Vault or K8s sealed-secrets configured.

Terraform module notes (observability module):
- Module layout suggested:
  - modules/observability/
    - main.tf (k8s provider, helm_release resources)
    - variables.tf (inputs)
    - outputs.tf

- Key variables (keep names stable to minimize drift):
  - cluster_name (string) - for naming conventions
  - monitoring_namespace (string, default: "redwood-observability")
  - prometheus_retention (string, default: "15d")
  - prometheus_storage (map) - {class = "fast-ssd", size = "200Gi"}
  - grafana_admin_password_secret (string) - vault path/secret id
  - otel_collector_image (string) - image:tag pinned
  - remote_write_enabled (bool) - default: false
  - remote_write_endpoint (string) - only used if enabled
  - enable_loki (bool) - default: true
  - log_storage_class (string)

- Recommended outputs:
  - grafana_url
  - prometheus_endpoint
  - otel_collector_endpoint
  - loki_write_endpoint

- Version pinning: pin Helm charts and OCI images in variables; do not rely on latest. Example: prometheus-operator chart v0.62.0, grafana 8.5.x.

- IAM / RBAC considerations:
  - Use a dedicated k8s service account for the module with least privilege for CRDs (ServiceMonitor, Prometheus, Alertmanager).
  - For cloud-managed clusters, create IAM role mapping for the service account when remote write to cloud targets is required.

Best-practice Helm values to set (summary):
- prometheus.operator: enablePodMonitoring = true, scrapeInterval = "30s", resources limits set to avoid eviction.
- prometheus.prometheusSpec: retention: from prometheus_retention variable, storageSpec using PVC template.
- grafana: adminPassword from secret, ingress disabled, internal service type ClusterIP, persistence enabled for dashboards.
- otelCollector: mode = deployment/daemonset configurable, receivers: prometheus, otlp; exporters: logging/local-loki/remote.

OTEL Collector recommendations:
- Mode selection: use DaemonSet for low-latency host metrics/traces collection; use a middle-tier deployment (receiver/processor/exporter) for sampling and batching prior to remote-write to save egress and cost.
- Batching: exporter: batch with max_export_batch_size = 1024 and timeout = 10s.
- Sampling: implement probabilistic sampling for traces above 1 request/s heat spots. Default bracket 0.01 (1%).
- Common receivers: otlp (4317/gRPC), prometheus, jaeger/zipkin optional.
- Recommended config snippet (plain text HCL/YAML in module repo): keep collector config in a ConfigMap referenced by the helm chart and make it templated by terraform variables.

Log shipping strategy:
- Use FluentBit on each node (DaemonSet) to tail container stdout, add k8s metadata, and forward to either Loki (preferred for Grafana) or Elasticsearch.
- Provide two shipping modes in module: local-loki (ClusterIP Loki) OR remote-elastic (remote HTTPS with basic auth or API key from vault).
- For sensitive logs, enable PII scrubbing filter (regex) in FluentBit and route to a separate secure index/bucket.

Prometheus specifics:
- Scrape targets: ServiceMonitor for all redwood services; additional static scrape configs for node-exporter and kube-state-metrics.
- Relabeling: drop metrics with label beta.kubernetes.io/os if not required; normalize job and instance labels to avoid high-cardinality labels.
- Federation/long-term: prefer Thanos sidecar or remote-write to S3-compatible bucket with retention; if remote_write is enabled, ensure credentials stored in sealed-secrets and exported to Prometheus via envFrom.

Grafana and Dashboards:
- Use Grafana provisioning to ship JSON dashboards via config map on deploy. Keep default dashboards minimal: node, kube-state, app-latency, otel-traces-sampled.
- Dashboards should be versioned in repo/terraform module and imported on upgrade (idempotent import).

Upgrade plan (observability stack) - safe path (step-by-step):
1) Preflight (2 days before):
   - Run terraform plan in staging; diff only changes in helm values or image tags.
   - Check cluster capacity: ensure extra 20% CPU/memory headroom for rolling upgrades.
   - Export current Prometheus/Thanos block metadata and snapshot: prometheus-cli snapshot command.
   - Backup Grafana DB (sqlite or PVC snapshot).
   - Notify stakeholders + maintenance window.
2) Stage rollout in canary namespace:
   - Apply helm chart changes for OTEL daemonset with new image tag; verify collectors register and metrics flow to Prometheus.
   - Run smoke tests: quick queries to Prometheus, ingest trace via curl otlp endpoint, check logs all collectors run.
3) Rolling upgrade across nodes:
   - Upgrade FluentBit DaemonSet with maxUnavailable: 1 to avoid downtime; watch logs for parse errors.
   - Upgrade Prometheus operator via Helm: monitor CR status, ensure new Prometheus pods become Ready before scale down old.
   - If using Thanos, upgrade sidecars in the same minor window to avoid TSDB incompatibilities.
4) Post-upgrade validation (24h):
   - Confirm retention, no missing series, and dashboards show recent data.
   - Check alerting rules firing frequency for false positives.

Rollback plan (if metrics lost or Grafana broken):
- Step 1: Rollback Helm release to previous chart revision: helm rollback <release> <rev>.
- Step 2: For Prometheus corruption, restore snapshot and reapply PVC claims.
- Step 3: Revert terraform variables to previous state and apply. Keep last-known good config committed.

Testing & verification checklist (post-upgrade):
- Prometheus: query series_count() and topk(10, sum by(job)(rate(http_requests_total[5m])))
- OTEL: generate a synthetic trace using the test client and search ID in Grafana/Tempo or Jaeger UI.
- Logs: tail last-1h logs in Loki for a sample pod, ensure labels present.

Security and compliance notes:
- Encrypt all secrets at rest using cluster KMS and use sealed-secrets for gitops.
- All remote-write traffic must use mTLS; validate cert rotation path before upgrade.
- Ensure RBAC grants only ServiceAccount access to watch custom resources (ServiceMonitor, prometheus).

Runbook: common incidents and quick fixes:
- Symptom: Prometheus stalled (not scraping) -> check ServiceMonitor CRs, prometheus operator logs, and disk pressure on PVs.
- Symptom: OTEL collector high CPU -> reduce receivers sampling rate, increase batching timeout, consider move from DaemonSet to middle-tier.
- Symptom: Logs missing -> check FluentBit config parse rules; confirm read permissions for /var/log/containers.

Migration notes (hosted -> private):
- Sanity: enable remote_write=false on first import to avoid double-writing to hosted backend.
- Export dashboards from hosted Grafana as JSON and import into private Grafana via provisioning.

Open questions / TODOs (follow-up work):
- Finalize Grafana admin password secret rotation automation (CRONJob using Vault).
- Standardize OTEL sampling policy templates per service class (low/medium/high).
- Add automated canary tests integrated into terraform apply pipeline (smoke harness that queries metrics).

Short checklist for terraform commit to do a first deploy:
- [ ] Add monitoring namespace variable and set default.
- [ ] Pin chart versions in variables.tf.
- [ ] Add grafana dashboard provisioning directory under module.
- [ ] Add sealed-secret manifest template for remote_write credentials.
- [ ] Add docs/upgrade-playbook.md in module repo linking this runbook.

Notes & references (quick links):
- Prometheus Operator docs: https://prometheus-operator.dev/
- OpenTelemetry Collector: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/
- Loki: https://grafana.com/oss/loki/

This document is intentionally a working draft. Use it as a source of truth for the first implementation and iterate after the staging rollout. Add checklists and exact configuration snippets to the module repo as separate files to keep terraform plan diffs small.
